title: Migrating Zscaler Service Admins to Authentication Service

blocks.text: Authentication Service (formerly ZIdentity) migration includes customer-driven migration. Customers that authenticate their Zscaler administrators with an external IdP can request for Authentication Service migration.

blocks.item: Customers must contact their Zscaler Account team to provision an Authentication Service tenant and have it linked to all their Zscaler tenants.

Zscaler sends an email to the customer to specify the Zscaler service tenants that must be linked to the Authentication Service tenant and the new Authentication Service super admin’s name and email ID.
Zscaler provisions the Authentication Service tenant and links the customer’s Zscaler service tenants (Internet & SaaS (ZIA), Private Access (ZPA), Digital Experience (ZDX), etc.).
Next, as the Authentication Service super admin, you need to complete the following:
When you receive the email about the new Authentication Service tenant registration, follow the instructions provided in the email and complete the registration.
Connect your organization's external IdP to Authentication Service and provision your admins (users) to Authentication Service.
Inform the other admins to test Authentication Service by clicking the tile at their IdP to confirm they see the Authentication Service SSO and the assigned Zscaler service tiles.
The service tiles are disabled until you complete the migration.

If the admins don't see the assigned tiles, the super admin can review the entitlements assigned to the admins on the Entitlements tab in the Authentication Service Admin Portal. They can also make adjustments to the entitlements on the Administrative Entitlements page.

When all the admins confirm they can access Authentication Service and see the Zscaler service tiles, go to the Zscaler Admin Console and click the link in the banner to proceed with the admin migration.
See image.
Read the message and click Confirm.
See image.
The Authentication Service admin migration is completed.

blocks.text: Authentication Service is the common identity service for all Zscaler products. Authentication Service provides a centralized platform for managing admin roles and entitlements across all Zscaler services. Authentication Service is being provisioned for all new customers since January 2024. Existing customers began upgrading to Authentication Service in June 2024. At this time, the majority of Zscaler customers are upgraded to Authentication Service.

If your organization uses Unified Role-Based Access Control (RBAC), administrator roles for Authentication Service and some Zscaler services are managed on a different Role Management page. To learn more, see About Role Management. Unified RBAC is a feature in limited availability. To access Unified RBAC, contact your Zscaler Account team.

Prior to Authentication Service, customers provisioned and managed administrators and end users directly in individual Zscaler services (e.g., Internet & SaaS (ZIA), Private Access (ZPA)). The external identity provider (IdP) integrations were also configured directly for individual Zscaler services.

blocks.item: With Authentication Service migration, administrator data and their role assignments are transferred from various Zscaler services and synced to Authentication Service. It also offers a unified authentication experience. Administrators can authenticate and access all Zscaler service admin portals with a single set of credentials, eliminating the need for multiple login credentials.

Authentication Service creates a default super admin account for tenant recoverability. This account cannot be deleted or disabled and is intended only for emergency (break-glass) use. Use named admin accounts for daily operations.

blocks.text: All administrators must use multi-factor authentication (MFA). You can either use Zscaler's MFA or enforce MFA with your external IdP, or both. Administrators hosted in Authentication Service are required to use Zscaler's MFA, as they are not using single sign-on (SSO) with an external IdP.

The authentication process changes after the admins are migrated to Authentication Service. After the migration, the credential validation for admins of all Zscaler services is handled by Authentication Service.
To improve security, all admins with credentials hosted at Zscaler must use MFA for admin login. The MFA options supported include security key or biometric, Google Authenticator, and email OTP.
Admins can authenticate in any of the following ways:
Zscaler recommends using a vanity domain (e.g., https://acme.zslogin.net) for simplicity and directly accessing Authentication Service via SSO URL.

blocks.item: Use the Two-Step Login Process
Access a Zscaler admin portal (Internet & SaaS, Private Access, ZDX, Branch Connector, Cloud Connector, or Deception).
Enter the login ID that you have been using.

After the migration, the credential validation for Internet & SaaS and Private Access admins is handled by Authentication Service. When Internet & SaaS or Private Access admins log in for the first time post migration, their password stored in the respective admin-portal is synced with the Authentication Service Admin Portal, and the validation is handled by Authentication Service.
Click Next.
Enter your existing password for the respective Zscaler service, then click Next.
When you are prompted to set up the MFA, select the required authentication method, then click Set Up.
See image.
A message appears indicating that a link is sent to your email address for completing MFA enrollment.
See image.
Click Continue and you are logged in to the respective admin portal.
Access Authentication Service through Your Organization's External IdP
Go to your organization's external IdP (e.g., Okta).
Click the Zscaler tile.
The Authentication Service page appears.
Enter the password that you have been using.
After successful validation, the Authentication Service page appears that displays the assigned Zscaler service tiles.
Zscaler recommends accepting the End User Service Agreement (EUSA), if it appears. You can access the Authentication Service page only if someone from your service tenant accepts the EUSA.
Use the Authentication Service Vanity Domain
Access the Zscaler assigned vanity domain (e.g., https://acme.zslogin.net).
The Authentication Service page appears.
Enter the login ID and password that you have been using.
You are prompted to set up the MFA.
After successful validation, the Authentication Service page appears that displays the assigned Zscaler service tiles.
Zscaler recommends accepting the End User Service Agreement (EUSA), if it appears. You can access the Authentication Service page only if someone from your service tenant accepts the EUSA.
Use Internet & SaaS Admin API and Zscaler Cloud & Branch Connectors

When Cloud & Branch Connector attempts to authenticate to Internet & SaaS's admin API and Internet & SaaS is linked to Authentication Service, Internet & SaaS receives the request and then attempts to validate the credentials with Authentication Service. If Authentication Service has a hosted user with that username and password, it validates the credentials and provides a successful response to Internet & SaaS. Then, Internet & SaaS responds to Cloud & Branch Connector with a success message, completing the admin API authentication.
User accounts with login ID domains that are associated with an external IdP can still be used for the Cloud & Branch Connector use case in some scenarios.

Authentication Service does not support users with both IdP mapping and passwords. However, to provide a seamless migration experience, passwords from Internet & SaaS are still synced to Authentication Service even if the user's domain is mapped to an IdP, retaining some password-managed functions. Additionally, Zscaler recommends that customers migrate away from such configurations where users with both password and IdP mapping are present. Customers must make necessary changes to use user identities under a vanity domain (e.g., <your_domain>.zslogin.net) that cannot be mapped against an IdP.

blocks.heading: Password Management and User Sync Behavior with External IdPs

blocks.text: If admins were originally synced from Internet & SaaS or Cloud & Branch Connector and an admin API authentication attempt was performed using their old passwords to Internet & SaaS Admin Portal or Cloud & Branch Connector Admin Portal, then Authentication Service requests Internet & SaaS or Cloud & Branch Connector services to look for the local password and copies it to Authentication Service to validate the current and subsequent API authentication calls. In such cases, Authentication Service enables the option to change passwords for admins even if their login ID domain is mapped to an external IdP. The options to change passwords in such cases are described as follows:

blocks.item: Admins synced to Authentication Service through external IdPs can change their passwords directly from the My Profile page in the Authentication Service Admin Portal.
See image.

Admins with the Users and Groups permission in Authentication Service roles can change passwords for users and admins synced from an external IdP by editing the corresponding user entry in the directory.
See image.
If Authentication Service does not maintain a local password for admins based on the API authentication event, then this option to change local passwords is not supported.

The password management functions for users and admins synced to Authentication Service via external IdPs only work when the identities are synced to Authentication Service from downstream services (e.g., Cloud & Branch Connector). For identities provisioned from external IdPs via SCIM or JIT provisioning, the password management functions are not supported.

blocks.text: For existing customers, identities might not get synced if they are removed from Authentication Service during the migration process. A support ticket must be raised to force sync the users from the downstream service. This synchronization issue occurs in the following scenario:

blocks.item: Authentication Service is in the provisioned state.
An IdP is configured for Authentication Service.
A user is deleted from Authentication Service Admin Portal manually.
Admin migration is completed with Zscaler services.
